title: District Explorer metro worksheet
description: One per fork (docs/MECHANIZATION_PLAYBOOK.md, Conversion 2). The single machine-readable source every per-fork GENERATED region is emitted from by scripts/generate_metro_files.py. A malformed worksheet fails validation before any file is touched.

this_metro.description: Key into metro_explorers; drops the fork's own entry from the rendered list.

permalink_gate.description: Greater metro area, wider than metro_bbox.

poi_geocode_bbox.description: OPTIONAL. Envelope the POI (office-address) geocoder is bounded to; defaults to metro_bbox when absent, which is the old behaviour and the right answer for a fork whose layers are all city-scoped. Set it only when a layer can name an address OUTSIDE metro_bbox — the bound tracks the reach of the fork's WIDEST layer, and one tighter than the data silently drops those pins however clean the address is. Chicago's county-clerk card answers statewide, so Chicago sets Illinois.

socrata_app_token.description: A Socrata app token is a public throttling identifier, not a secret — never put an API Key secret here. Empty string = requests sent anonymous.

metro_explorers.description: The fleet list, identical in every fork. Conversion 3 will source this from the canonical fleet manifest (chidistricts.com/metros.json) at generation time; until then it is authored here.

explorer_name.description: Optional display name for this sibling's app (e.g. a rebranded fork). Absent = the engine's historical composition (label + " District Explorer") stands; present = emitted onto the METRO_EXPLORERS entry for the engine to prefer. Sourced from metros.json by --sync-fleet when the manifest carries it.

layers.description: Every registered layer, in LAYER_AREA_RANK order (largest real-world area first). Drives EXPECT_LAYER_IDS, the index.html LAYER_AREA_RANK array, and the smoke test's layer count.

rank_note.description: Inline // comment on the LAYER_AREA_RANK entry.

rank_comment.description: Full-line // comment block emitted immediately before the entry (ordering rationale).

source.description: Reader-facing provenance for this layer, rendered as one row of the public sources page's layer matrix. Optional per layer, but a fork that sets sources_page must supply it for EVERY layer — a matrix with a blank row is worse than no matrix, because a reader reads the blank as 'no source'.

answers.description: One sentence, in a reader's words, naming what question this layer answers.

boundary.description: Where the geometry comes from. Several entries when a layer dispatches across publishers (the county concept layers).

url.description: The publisher's own page for this dataset. Omit when the source has no citable public page (a licensed file, a pre-built derivation); the label then stands alone.

people.description: Where the officeholder names on this layer's card come from, or an honest statement that the layer names nobody. Omitted only when the concept has no officeholder at all.

applies.description: Where the layer answers at all, in plain words — the reader-facing form of the layer's coverage() test.

guide.description: Optional. A per-concept explainer page in this instance that answers the layer's own question in prose — /il/police-district.html and its five siblings. Declaring it here links the layer's sources.html row AND the app footer from ONE key, so a new explainer is linked on both surfaces by adding this block rather than by remembering two files. Measured 2026-09-11: no instance hub or sources page linked any of the six, and they were reachable only through faq.html.

href.description: Filename relative to the instance folder, e.g. police-district.html.

text.description: Anchor text, written to match the question the target page answers — that is what the link is worth to a reader and to a crawler, where a row of "Guide" links describes nothing.

min_register_layer.description: validate_index.py floor for the raw registerLayer( count. New layers only raise it.

layer_count_note.description: Optional inline comment on the smoke test's EXPECT_LAYERS constant.

anchors.description: >=3 API-free anchor layers with the district each one must report at anchor_point.

negative_point.description: A point where every anchor layer reports no district.

dynamic_reference.description: True when the app references this file DYNAMICALLY (URL built from a slug at runtime, e.g. the gaps panel's <slug>-county-outline.json contract) — exempts it from validate_index's literal-reference check only; existence/shape checks still apply.

True when the app references this file DYNAMICALLY (URL built from a slug at runtime, e.g. the ward card's <slug>-polling-places.json contract) — exempts it from validate_index's literal-reference check only; existence/shape checks still apply. Already allowed on geometry entries; rosters need it too, because a per-county roster is addressed the same way a per-county outline is.

cache_name.description: Full CACHE_NAME including version suffix; bump the suffix when shell contents change.

data_sources.description: Either a pointer to the fork's machine-checked source registry (preferred — scripts/validate_sources.py already guards manifest<->app drift; a second copy here would just drift against it), or literal registry rows for a fork that has no validator yet.

workflows.description: This fork's scraper/builder + freshness workflows with schedules.

geocoder.description: Provider names for the three fork-defined functions (geocodeAddress / geocodeUnbounded / poiGeocodeRequest). Descriptive — the provider code itself is fork code by design.

search_placeholder.description: The words in the search box and in its visually-hidden label. OPTIONAL: the shared toolbar ships a neutral default ("Search an address"), so a new instance is correct before anyone writes this and setting it is a refinement rather than a step that can be forgotten. Not derivable from metro_name — Chicago's box says "an Illinois address", not "a Chicago address", and the article changes with the name.

label.description: One-line provenance of the palette (e.g. "Chicago flag palette"), printed as the comment heading the generated :root accent block. Only read when the brand key opts the fork into the generated palette regions.

notes.description: Optional per-token comment printed beside the generated :root line for that token.

exports_name.description: window.<name> debug namespace, twinned with the smoke test.

coverage_key.description: Opts this instance into the COVERAGE KEY — the legend that reads the out-of-scope wash on the map. The wash is the app's only claim about where it stops answering, and without a key it makes that claim in a colour with nothing to read it against. The BANDS are engine and identical everywhere; only their names differ, which is what this key supplies. Absent = the wash still draws and no key is built, so an instance that has not opted in sees a byte-identical metro-config region.

outside.description: Names the washed band OUTSIDE this instance's coverage, in the reader's terms (e.g. "Outside Illinois", "Outside San Francisco"). NOT derivable from metro_name: Chicago's metro_name is "Chicago" while its coverage is 89 Illinois counties, so "Outside Chicago" would be plainly wrong.

region.description: The MIDDLE band, for an instance whose full coverage is a proper SUBSET of a wider region its statewide layers still answer in. Illinois is the only one today: its county layers cover 89 counties while county/township/municipality/school-district/ZIP answer anywhere in the state. Omit it when coverage IS the whole region (Wisconsin) or there is no wider region in play (San Francisco, New York City) — then the wash is two bands and the key names two. Declaring this also requires the instance's boot to pass the region geometry to drawOutOfScopeMask(); a label with no geometry draws no band, and the key names only bands that were drawn.

edge.description: Names the glowing region boundary itself (e.g. "Illinois").

label.description: Names the middle band — what a reader still gets there (e.g. "Statewide layers only").

sub.description: Optional second line saying what is MISSING there (e.g. "County board and local districts not sourced yet").

brand.description: Opts this fork into brand-as-data (docs/DEV_PROCESS_ASSESSMENT.md, stage R1): the generator owns the brand-bearing GENERATED regions (head-analytics, head-brand, head-theme, brand-palette, masthead-brand, goatcounter in index.html; sources-palette on the sources page when sources_page is also set) and emits METRO_BRAND into the metro-config region. Absent = every one of those surfaces stays hand-written and the generator emits nothing new, which is what keeps this key inert in a fork that has not opted in.

app_name.description: This instance's display name (masthead title, og:site_name; e.g. "Chicago District Explorer").

product_name.description: The product's brand name shared across instances (e.g. "districtry"). Optional until a rebrand consumes it; emitted onto METRO_BRAND when present.

instance_tag.description: The wordmark's instance suffix (e.g. "il"). Optional until a rebrand consumes it; emitted onto METRO_BRAND when present.

jsonld.description: Opts this instance into a GENERATED ld+json graph on index.html. The graph was hand-written six times and every field that is CONSTANT across the fleet (the publisher, the licence-free Offer, the browser requirements, inLanguage) was six chances to differ; measured 2026-09-11 all nine agreed, and they are literals in the generator now so they cannot stop agreeing. Everything derivable — @id, url, name, image, isPartOf, publisher — comes from the instance tag and brand.app_name. What is left is the four values below, which are genuinely this instance's own prose. dateModified is emitted from verified_date, which is why this block exists at all: the audit asked for it and nothing could carry it while the graph was hand-written.

site_description.description: WebSite.description — what the SITE is, one sentence.

app_description.description: WebApplication.description — what the APP does. Longer than the SERP description and not the same string; this one is not truncated at 155.

area_served.description: Where the app answers. A city instance names its city AND its state and renders as a City containedInPlace a State; a statewide instance names the state alone and renders as a State. The generator picks the @type, so an instance cannot declare a shape schema.org does not have.

tagline.description: The masthead's one-line subtitle under the title.

favicon_data_uri.description: The favicon as an inline data: URI, exactly as the <link rel="icon"> href should carry it.

apple_touch_icon.description: Instance-relative href for <link rel="apple-touch-icon"> (e.g. "icons/apple-touch-icon.png"; NY's icons live under "icons/app/"). iOS ignores the web app manifest's icons entirely when adding to the Home Screen and reads only this tag, so without it an iPhone install has no branded icon to use. The file must be 180x180 and FULLY OPAQUE — iOS composites a transparent apple-touch-icon onto black, and it applies its own corner mask, so the artwork is full-bleed with no rounding of its own. Optional: omit it and no tag is emitted, which is the pre-existing behaviour for a fork that has not shipped the asset.

analytics.description: OPTIONAL, and every key inside it is optional too. A brand block used to REQUIRE this object with a ga_id, which meant adopting the districtry brand FORCED Google Analytics onto the app — including SF, which ships none today and whose readers have never been sent to Google. A rebrand must not add a tracker, so each surface is independently opt-in: the generator emits the GA snippet only when ga_id and ga_hostname are both present, and the GoatCounter tag only when goatcounter_url is. The dependentRequired below keeps the one real coupling — a ga_id with no hostname gate would fire on local dev, CI and previews, which is exactly what that gate exists to prevent.

ga_hostname.description: The production hostname the GA snippet gates on — analytics never fire on local dev, CI, or previews.

verified_date.description: The date the app claims its data was last verified, in the prose form both surfaces print (e.g. "August 3, 2026"). Optional: a fork that omits it keeps its hand-written date in index.html and generates nothing. Setting it takes over the verified-date region in index.html AND the sources page's header, so one bump moves both.

sources_page.description: Opts this fork into a public sources page. Present = the generator owns the page's GENERATED regions and every layer must carry a source block; absent = the page and its regions are skipped entirely, which is what keeps this key inert in a fork that has not opted in.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the page carrying the GENERATED regions (e.g. "sources.html").

credits.description: The upstream publishers the app credits as a whole — the list that used to be the footer's source row. Per-layer provenance belongs in layers[].source, not here.

note.description: Optional half-sentence on what this publisher supplies.

history_page.description: Opts this instance into a generated deployment-history page (scripts/build_history_page.py). Present = the generator owns <instance>/<file> and index.html must link it; absent = no page is generated and --check fails on an orphaned history.html. entries are DATED, newest-first, append-only narrative snapshots; metrics restate shipped data/app files through a tiny measure vocabulary so a stat tile can never drift from the data it counts.

perf_profile.description: Opts this fork's performance harness into the generated perf-config region (the anchor point + offline layer list that must mirror smoke-config). Present = the generator owns that region in the named file; absent = no target, byte-identical output (the verified_date pattern).

groupedKeys.description: Array of line-groups: each inner array renders as one source line, preserving the hand-grouped readability of the key lists.
